stated: Establish a powerful new Worker Protection Enforcement Authority unifying responsibilities currently spread across three agencies – including enforcing the minimum wage, tackling modern slavery and protecting agency workers.

source.quote: Establish a powerful new Worker Protection Enforcement Authority unifying responsibilities currently spread across three agencies – including enforcing the minimum wage, tackling modern slavery and protecting agency workers.

bearing_set.reason: Unifying enforcement of minimum wage compliance and agency worker protections directly affects whether workers receive fair pay and secure, lawful employment conditions.

Explicitly includes tackling modern slavery, which is a serious organised crime; consolidated enforcement authority would directly affect detection, prosecution, and dismantling of criminal exploitation networks.

Stronger enforcement of minimum wage and agency-worker protections concentrates gains at the bottom of the wage distribution, mechanically narrowing the gap between low-paid and higher-paid workers — a direct O14 indicator.

membership_note: The policy is a labour-market enforcement consolidation with three real, non-negligible effects: improved working conditions (O4), reduced serious criminality (O5), and a narrowing of the wage gap via targeted enforcement at the low-pay end (O14). Fiscal cost of consolidating three agencies into one is broadly neutral and does not earn a real O12 verdict. O9 was considered but the mechanism here is labour and criminal law enforcement, not anti-discrimination law specifically — O4 and O5 already capture the substantive effects on vulnerable groups.
